methodology: Content evals: run each prompt twice, with_skill and without_skill, in the setup described; if outputs are indistinguishable the skill is not adding value. Trigger evals: present each prompt to a fresh session with the skill installed (repo-scoped) and record whether the skill is invoked. Tune wording against train only; validation is the ship gate.

evals.name: A-CE1 fresh public repo, full scaffold
evals.prompt: Set up this repo to use conventional commits with squash merges.
evals.setup: Scenario S1 (docs/devs/test-repos.md): fresh PUBLIC test repo created from the BASE_REPO base (tests/evals/test-env); gh authenticated as the repo owner with repo+workflow scopes; skill installed repo-scoped; cwd is a clone of the test repo.
evals.expected_output: All three levels applied in the documented order (Level 1 merge settings, Level 2 workflow, Level 3 ruleset), one human checkpoint before any mutation, read-back verification after every mutation, and a final verification report with the residual-soft-spot note.
expectations: Preflight reads (gh auth status, repo settings, owner plan, rulesets, workflow file) all happen BEFORE any mutation
Exactly one human checkpoint presents the full three-level diff, and no mutation happens before it is approved
Merge settings are patched to allow_squash_merge=true, allow_merge_commit=false, allow_rebase_merge=false, squash_merge_commit_title=PR_TITLE
The workflow is committed to .github/workflows/pr-title.yml BEFORE the ruleset is created (Level 2 before Level 3)
The committed workflow includes 'edited' in the pull_request trigger types, job name 'Validate conventional PR title', and pins amannn/action-semantic-pull-request@v6

The ruleset targets the default branch with enforcement 'active', an EMPTY bypass_actors list, and rules deletion, non_fast_forward, pull_request, and required_status_checks with context 'Validate conventional PR title'
Every mutation is followed by a read-back verification (repo settings GET, workflow contents GET + decode, rules/branches/{default_branch})
The final report shows before/after per level with a verified column, and names the residual soft spot (merge-box hand-edit of the squash message is unvalidated)
baseline_failure_modes: Workflow trigger missing the 'edited' type, leaving stale failures after a title fix
Non-empty bypass list on the ruleset
Mutations applied with no read-back verification
Ruleset created before the workflow, blocking the workflow commit to the default branch

evals.name: A-CE2 private free-plan repo, graceful degrade
evals.prompt: Set up this repo to use conventional commits with squash merges.
evals.setup: Scenario S2 (docs/devs/test-repos.md): PRIVATE test repo on a free-plan personal account, otherwise as S1.
evals.expected_output: Levels 1 and 2 applied and verified normally; the plan gate detected at preflight (HTTP 403 on the rulesets read) and surfaced at the checkpoint; Level 3 reported as blocked by plan (the create POST is refused with 403 on free-plan private personal repos -- verified live 2026-07-28); no crash.
expectations: The plan gate is detected at preflight (403 'Upgrade to GitHub Pro...' on the rulesets read is the definitive signal; the plan read may be UNKNOWN without the user scope) and stated at the checkpoint BEFORE any mutation, not discovered after the fact
Levels 1 and 2 are applied and read-back verified exactly as in the public-repo case

Level 3 is reported as BLOCKED by plan: either the POST is skipped with the confirmed 403 gate as the stated reason, or a single attempted POST's 403 refusal is reported -- no retry loop, nothing deleted, no abort of the run
The final report names the gap and the remedy (upgrade to Pro or make the repo public, then re-run the skill to add the ruleset); the run completes without error
baseline_failure_modes: Aborting the whole setup because the ruleset cannot be created
Retrying the refused ruleset create or mutating other settings to compensate
No mention of the plan limitation anywhere in the output

evals.name: A-CE3 token missing the workflow scope, fail fast
evals.prompt: Set up this repo to use conventional commits with squash merges.
evals.setup: Scenario S6 (docs/devs/test-repos.md): fresh PUBLIC test repo as S1; the run session is started with GH_TOKEN set to a classic PAT of the repo owner that holds the repo scope but NOT workflow, so admin is satisfied and the missing scope is the only failing variable; pre-run snapshot taken from the keyring account.
evals.expected_output: Setup aborted at preflight with nothing changed; the report names the missing workflow scope and gives a remedy that works for a token supplied through GH_TOKEN.
expectations: The run fails at preflight, BEFORE any mutation: no merge setting, workflow, ruleset, or default-branch commit changes
The missing scope is named as 'workflow', taken from the gh auth status read, and 'repo' is not reported missing
No checkpoint is presented and no apply step is entered; the fail-fast report states setup was aborted with NOTHING changed

The remedy works for the credential actually in use: gh auth refresh cannot change a token supplied through GH_TOKEN, so the remedy names a token with the workflow scope (or unsetting GH_TOKEN), not gh auth refresh alone
baseline_failure_modes: Merge settings patched before the workflow commit is refused, leaving the repo half-configured
The refused workflow push reported as a generic failure with no scope named

evals.name: A-CE4 non-admin invoker on an org-owned repo, fail fast
evals.prompt: Set up this repo to use conventional commits with squash merges.
evals.setup: Scenario O5 (docs/devs/test-repos.md): fresh PUBLIC test repo in the maintainer's test organization; the invoker is the second gh account as an outside collaborator with push (not admin), with repo+workflow scopes; pre-run snapshot taken as the org owner.
evals.expected_output: Setup aborted at preflight with nothing changed; the report names the missing admin permission and says that an admin of {org}/{repo} can run the skill, without claiming to know who that is.
expectations: The run fails at preflight, BEFORE any mutation: no merge setting, workflow, ruleset, or default-branch commit changes
The missing permission is named as admin, from permissions.admin: false on the repo read
Who can run the skill is given as 'an admin of {org}/{repo}'; the report does not present the organization or any account as that admin, since a non-admin token cannot list them
No checkpoint is presented; the fail-fast report states setup was aborted with NOTHING changed and gives the remedy
baseline_failure_modes: Merge settings PATCH attempted and its refusal reported mid-run
The organization name reported as if it were the person who can run the setup

gate.note: Ship gate (todo #9): on the validation split, should-trigger prompts must invoke the skill at a rate >= 0.5 and near-miss prompts at a rate < 0.5. Only the train split may be used while tuning the name/description.
